clue.text: Rough one is carried by out-of-date transport

indicators.note: something carried by a vehicle sits inside it, so the first piece goes within the second

parts.note: the horse was the transport of earlier days, now superseded
a means one

explanation.surface: Something crude travels in an old-fashioned conveyance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is carried by' puts A inside HORSE.
explanation.definitionFit: A rough voice is a husky, croaky one, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Fish had to reach harbour

parts.note: taken as written
a dock is a harbour area for ships

explanation.surface: A fisherman had to make it to port.
explanation.definitionFit: The haddock is a North Atlantic food fish related to cod.

clue.text: Viper with a different tail, it is calculated

indicators.note: a different tail means the last letter is swapped for another one

parts.note: the adder is Britain's only venomous snake, a viper

explanation.surface: A snake with an odd tail, and it's been sized up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with a different tail' changes the final R of ADDER to D.
explanation.definitionFit: Added means summed up, so worked out or calculated.

clue.text: Assistant, disguised, sticks to a railway

parts.note: something disguised is kept hidden, secret

explanation.surface: An aide in disguise clings to a railway line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disguised' looks like an anagram signal; it is SECRET.
explanation.definitionFit: A secretary is an office assistant handling correspondence and records.

clue.text: The hobby of father's generation, say

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father, with the possessive S
a generation is a period or era, a time

explanation.surface: A pursuit that belonged to Dad's era.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' hints that the pieces read as a phrase: father's time.
explanation.definitionFit: A pastime is a leisure activity, a straightforward synonym of hobby.

clue.text: Last course for a fat person

definitions.meaning: the dessert served at the end of a meal
an informal, affectionate term for a plump, stout person

explanation.surface: The final dish is meant for someone overweight.
explanation.definitionFit: Pudding means dessert in British usage and is also slang for a podgy person.

clue.text: A swindle is no good after it's mounted

indicators.note: the abbreviation comes after the turned word
in a down clue, mounted means raised up, so the word reads upwards

parts.note: taken as written, the apostrophe giving no letter

explanation.surface: A con trick fails once it has been set up.
explanation.definitionFit: A sting is slang for an elaborate confidence trick, a swindle.

clue.text: Charged upwards of half when squeezing fruit

indicators.note: squeezing means pressing around, so one piece encloses the other
in a down clue upwards means the word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: demi is a prefix meaning half
a peach is a fruit

explanation.surface: Somebody accused of squashing fruit by half its weight.
explanation.definitionFit: To be impeached is to be formally charged with misconduct in office.

clue.text: Call up some women listeners

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A recruiter phones a few female radio listeners.
explanation.definitionFit: To call up is to conscript someone into the forces, as enlisting does.

clue.text: Italian's daughter thought to have charisma, wealth and beauty

definitions.text: thought to have charisma, wealth and beauty

parts.note: IT is an abbreviation for Italian
a girl is a daughter

explanation.surface: An Italian's daughter is widely seen as glamorous and rich.
explanation.definitionFit: An it girl is a young woman famed for glamour and social prominence.

clue.text: Devoted half-dead moggy died outside

indicators.note: half of the four-letter word gives only its first two letters
died goes around the cat, enclosing it

parts.note: taken as written
moggy is British slang for an ordinary cat

explanation.surface: A loyal pet, half-dead, finally expires.
explanation.definitionFit: Dedicated and devoted both mean wholeheartedly committed, a synonym.

clue.text: Prod representative that is about 50

indicators.note: about means around, so the abbreviation surrounds the representative

parts.note: i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is
an MP is a Member of Parliament, an elected representative
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: Nudging a politician who is about fifty years old.
explanation.definitionFit: To impel someone is to drive or urge them on, the same as prod.

clue.text: Serviceman cannot start or finish, but he is getting on

indicators.note: losing the start and finish means the first and last letters are dropped

parts.note: a soldier is a serviceman in the army

explanation.surface: A veteran soldier, too old now to begin or end anything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cannot start or finish' strips S and R from SOLDIER.
explanation.definitionFit: An oldie is an informal word for an elderly person, one who is getting on in years.

clue.text: A fish product? I tell all to a girl

parts.note: to sing is slang for confessing everything to the police
lass is a northern British word for a girl

explanation.surface: A confession made to a young woman, oddly framed as seafood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tell all' is SING in its informer sense, not singing a tune.
explanation.definitionFit: Isinglass is a gelatine made from the swim bladders of fish, so a product of fish.

clue.text: Cleverdick king needs no barricade

parts.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king
taken as written
a wall is a barrier or barricade

explanation.surface: A smug monarch thinks he needs no defences.
explanation.definitionFit: A cleverdick and a know-all are both people who show off their supposed knowledge.

clue.text: Begin to speak pompously, having swallowed one drink

indicators.note: swallowing takes something inside, so one piece encloses the others

parts.note: to orate is to speak grandly or pompously
I is the Roman numeral one
gin is a drink

explanation.surface: A speaker launches into a pompous speech after a quick gin.
explanation.definitionFit: To originate is to start or come into being, so begin.

clue.text: Cowboy wants to go round church after gold

indicators.note: go goes round the next pieces, enclosing them

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: church comes after gold in the inserted pair

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: A rancher wants to detour round a church once he has his gold.
explanation.definitionFit: A gaucho is a South American cowboy of the pampas.

clue.text: Sabotage controlled by explosive device

parts.note: under means subject to or controlled by
a mine is a buried explosive device

explanation.surface: Sabotage carried out with a bomb.
explanation.definitionFit: To undermine is to weaken by subversion, the same as to sabotage.

clue.text: DIY put off, but this is put in order

indicators.note: off means the letters have gone bad or awry, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Home improvements are postponed, yet the place still gets sorted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' looks like part of 'put off' meaning postpone; it signals the anagram of DIY PUT.
explanation.definitionFit: To tidy up something is to put it in order, a phrasal synonym.

clue.text: Flourish, but the right Duke of Milan has lost nothing

indicators.note: losing something means a letter is removed from the name

parts.note: Prospero is the rightful Duke of Milan in Shakespeare's The Tempest
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A deposed duke thrives despite losing everything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has lost' removes the final O from PROSPERO.
explanation.definitionFit: To prosper is to thrive or do well, synonymous with flourish.

clue.text: Gentlewoman has time for Christian feast

parts.note: a lady is a woman of good family, a gentlewoman
a day is a period of time

explanation.surface: A noblewoman makes time for a church festival.
explanation.walkthrough: LADY DAY is the Feast of the Annunciation on 25 March, also an old English quarter day.
explanation.definitionFit: The Annunciation festival on 25 March is a Christian feast day honouring Mary.

clue.text: Honour of good man in the grip of temptation

indicators.note: held in another's grip means the piece sits inside it

parts.note: a lure is an enticement or temptation
ST, short for saint, is the crossword good man

explanation.surface: A virtuous man's reputation is held by temptation.
explanation.definitionFit: Lustre can mean glory or distinction, a sense close to honour.

clue.text: Gave in with damaged eyelid, then died

indicators.note: damaged means broken up, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for died, used in genealogies

explanation.surface: Someone surrendered with a hurt eye, then passed away.
explanation.definitionFit: Yielded means surrendered or conceded, so gave in.

clue.text: Mushroom feast

definitions.meaning: as a verb, to grow or expand rapidly
an informal word for a lavish meal laid out

explanation.definitionFit: Spread means both to extend rapidly, like mushrooming, and a large meal set out on a table.

clue.text: Toxic soup I soon blended

indicators.note: blended means mixed together, so the letters are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: A cook liquidises some soup and finds it is poisonous.
explanation.definitionFit: Poisonous and toxic are direct synonyms for harmful substances.

clue.text: Blasphemy has to change

indicators.note: change says the letters are altered into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Profanity has to be reformed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change' rearranges HAS TO; 'to' is fodder, not a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Oaths are curses or profane swearing, which is blasphemy.

clue.text: Variety puts any number in a temper

indicators.note: in places the number inside the temper

parts.note: a rage is a fit of temper
n is the mathematical symbol for an unspecified number

explanation.surface: Variety shows can drive anyone into a fury.
explanation.definitionFit: A range is a varied selection, like a range of goods, so a variety.

clue.text: Whas a degree? I'm not a child!

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A grown-up protesting about academic qualifications.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue's 'Whas' is a typo for 'What's'.
explanation.definitionFit: A notch is a step or level on a scale, so a degree.

clue.text: Former wife gets to do something right

parts.note: an ex is a former spouse
to act is to take action, to do something

explanation.surface: A divorcee finally decides to set things right.
explanation.definitionFit: Exact means precisely correct, so right in the sense of accurate.

clue.text: Authorised instruction to Edward, the hairdresser?

parts.note: read with the next words this is an instruction to a hairdresser: perm it
Ted is a short form of Edward

explanation.surface: A salon order to Ted, the stylist, approves a curly style.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as 'Perm it, Ted!', an order to a hairdresser called Edward; 'the hairdresser' sets that scene and gives no letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Permitted and authorised both mean allowed by someone in charge.

clue.text: US novelist with eccentric desire to be next to river

indicators.note: eccentric means odd or off-centre, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An American writer with an odd longing to live beside a river.
explanation.definitionFit: Theodore Dreiser was an American novelist, author of Sister Carrie and An American Tragedy.

clue.text: Take me to the outhouse, having got engaged

parts.note: taken as written
a shed is an outhouse in a garden

explanation.surface: A proposal: take me to the garden shed, now we are betrothed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'engaged' suggests betrothal; here it is gears interlocking.
explanation.definitionFit: Gears that have meshed have locked together, the mechanical sense of engaged.
